docs.name: cas.google-recaptcha.verify-url
docs.description:
The reCAPTCHA endpoint for verification of the reCAPTCHA response. The endpoint is specific to the reCAPTCHA provider:
  • For Google reCAPTCHA, the endpoint is {@code https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify}.
  • For hCaptcha, the endpoint is {@code https://hcaptcha.com/siteverify}.
  • For Turnstile, the endpoint is {@code https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify}.

docs.name: cas.google-recaptcha.version
docs.description:
Indicate the version of the recaptcha api. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_V2}: V2 version of the recaptcha API.
  • {@code GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_V3}: V3 version of the recaptcha API.
  • {@code HCAPTCHA}: hCaptcha is an alternative to reCAPTCHA that requires website visitors to label images as part of its business model. The provider is more focused on manual image recognition challenges. It is a image classification task based CAPTCHA provider employing visual challenges like identifying objects.
  • {@code TURNSTILE}: Offers a CAPTCHA alternative by Cloudflare that prioritizes user experience and privacy. Turnstile delivers frustration-free, CAPTCHA-free web experiences to website visitors - with just a simple snippet of free code. Moreover, Turnstile stops abuse and confirms visitors are real without the data privacy concerns or awful user experience of CAPTCHAs.
  • {@code FRIENDLY_CAPTCHA}: Friendly captcha is a European alternative, accessible and GDPR compliant.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.allow-credentials
docs.description: The Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header Indicates whether or not the response to the request can be exposed when the credentials flag is true. When used as part of a response to a preflight request, this indicates whether or not the actual request can be made using credentials. Note that simple GET requests are not preflighted, and so if a request is made for a resource with credentials, if this header is not returned with the resource, the response is ignored by the browser and not returned to web content.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.allow-headers
docs.description: The Access-Control-Allow-Headers header is used in response to a preflight request to indicate which HTTP headers can be used when making the actual request. Default is everything.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.allow-methods
docs.description: The Access-Control-Allow-Methods header specifies the method or methods allowed when accessing the resource. This is used in response to a pre-flight request. The conditions under which a request is pre-flighted are discussed above. Default is everything.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.allow-origin-patterns
docs.description: Comma-separated list of origin patterns to allow. Unlike allowed origins which only supports {@code *}, origin patterns are more flexible (for example {@code https://*.example.com}) and can be used when credentials are allowed. When no allowed origin patterns or allowed origins are set, CORS support is disabled.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.allow-origins
docs.description: The Origin header indicates the origin of the cross-site access request or preflight request. The origin is a URI indicating the server from which the request initiated. When credentials are allowed, '*' cannot be used and origin patterns should be configured instead. It does not include any path information, but only the server name.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.enabled
docs.description: Whether CORS should be enabled for http requests.

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.exposed-headers

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.cors.max-age

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.custom-headers

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.header.cache

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.header.cache-control-static-resources

docs.name: cas.http-web-request.header.content-security-policy
docs.description: Helps you reduce XSS risks on modern browsers by declaring what dynamic resources are allowed to load via a HTTP Header. Header value is made up of one or more directives. Multiple directives are separated with a semicolon. @nonce@ is a specific value which is replaced by a generated random value saved as the request attribute 'contentSecurityPolicyGeneratedNonce'.
docs.defaultValue: script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://www.googletagmanager.com https://www.google.com; object-src 'none'; worker-src 'self' blob: 'unsafe-inline';

docs.name: cas.interrupt.cookie.pin-to-session
docs.description:
When generating cookie values, determine whether the value should be compounded and signed with the properties of the current session, such as IP address, user-agent, etc.

Turning off session pinning is not exactly ideal. This is a barrier to prevent cookie replay attacks. A cookie that was created with an IP given a certain location cannot be replayed back in a different browser with a different IP from a different location.

There may however be legitimate reasons to turn it off and relax this after careful reviews, if you intend to support a type of user who intends to switch their IP quite frequently. A classic example is the type of user that is on VPN at the time of login, but decides to resume their work a few hours later off VPN or at a different location.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.client-uri
docs.description: The connection uri to the mongodb instance. This typically takes on the form of {@code mongodb://user:psw@ds135522.somewhere.com:35522/db}. If not specified, will fallback onto other individual settings. If specified, takes over all other settings where applicable.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.database-name
docs.description: MongoDb database instance name.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.host
docs.description: MongoDb database host for authentication. Multiple host addresses may be defined, separated by comma. If more than one host is defined, it is assumed that each host contains the port as well, if any. Otherwise the configuration may fallback onto the port defined.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.password
docs.description: MongoDb database password for authentication.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.pool.idle-time
docs.description: The maximum idle time of a pooled connection. A zero value indicates no limit to the idle time. A pooled connection that has exceeded its idle time will be closed and replaced when necessary by a new connection.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.pool.life-time
docs.description: The maximum time a pooled connection can live for. A zero value indicates no limit to the life time. A pooled connection that has exceeded its life time will be closed and replaced when necessary by a new connection.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.pool.max-size
docs.description: Maximum number of connections to keep around.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.pool.max-wait-time
docs.description: The maximum time that a thread may wait for a connection to become available.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.pool.min-size
docs.description: Minimum number of connections to keep around.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.port
docs.description: MongoDb database port.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.read-concern
docs.description:
Read concern. Accepted values are:
  • {@code LOCAL}
  • {@code MAJORITY}
  • {@code LINEARIZABLE}
  • {@code SNAPSHOT}
  • {@code AVAILABLE}

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.read-preference
docs.description:
Read preference. Accepted values are:
  • {@code PRIMARY}
  • {@code SECONDARY}
  • {@code SECONDARY_PREFERRED}
  • {@code PRIMARY_PREFERRED}
  • {@code NEAREST}

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.replica-set
docs.description: A replica set in MongoDB is a group of {@code mongod} processes that maintain the same data set. Replica sets provide redundancy and high availability, and are the basis for all production deployments.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.retry-writes
docs.description: Sets whether writes should be retried if they fail due to a network error.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.ssl-enabled
docs.description: Whether connections require SSL.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.timeout
docs.description: MongoDb database connection timeout.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.user-id
docs.description: MongoDb database user for authentication.

docs.name: cas.javers.mongo.write-concern
docs.description: Write concern describes the level of acknowledgement requested from MongoDB for write operations to a standalone mongo db or to replica sets or to sharded clusters. In sharded clusters, mongo db instances will pass the write concern on to the shards.

docs.name: cas.jdbc.gen-ddl
docs.description: Whether to generate DDL after the EntityManagerFactory has been initialized creating/updating all relevant tables.

docs.name: cas.jdbc.physical-table-names
docs.description: Indicate a physical table name to be used by the hibernate naming strategy in case table names need to be customized for the specific type of database. The key here indicates the CAS-provided table name and the value is the translate physical name for the database. If a match is not found for the CAS-provided table name, then that name will be used by default.

docs.name: cas.jdbc.show-sql
docs.description: Whether SQL queries should be displayed in the console/logs.

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.domain
docs.description: Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented. The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com) and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com). By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.http-only
docs.description: true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.max-age
docs.description: The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating the cookie will persist until browser shutdown. A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age. A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.locale.cookie.secure
docs.description: True if sending this cookie should be restricted to a secure protocol, or false if the it can be sent using any protocol.

docs.description: Default locale.

docs.name: cas.locale.param-name

Each log group can have a unique name, and you can think of it as a logical grouping of logs that relate to a specific application, service, or environment.

docs.name: cas.logging.cloudwatch.log-stream-name
docs.description: A log stream is a sequence of log events that share the same source. Each log stream belongs to a log group, and you can have multiple log streams within a single log group. Log streams are typically used to separate log data from different sources within the same application or service.

docs.name: cas.logging.cloudwatch.proxy-username

docs.name: cas.logging.cloudwatch.region

docs.name: cas.logging.cloudwatch.retry-mode

docs.name: cas.logging.cloudwatch.socket-timeout

docs.name: cas.logging.gcp.labels

docs.name: cas.logging.gcp.log-name
docs.description:
In Google Cloud Logging, the log name is an identifier that specifies the particular log to which log entries are written or from which they are retrieved. It is an essential component when interacting with logs using the Google Cloud Logging API, as it allows you to target specific logs for querying or analysis.

It typically has the following syntax: {@code projects/[PROJECT_ID]/logs/[LOG_ID]}

docs.name: cas.logging.gcp.project-id
docs.description: A Project ID is a unique identifier assigned to a specific project within your GCP environment. The Project ID is globally unique across all GCP projects, meaning no two projects can have the same Project ID. The Project ID is used in various API calls, configurations, and URLs to uniquely identify your CAS project.

docs.name: cas.logging.mdc.enabled
docs.description: Allow CAS to add http request details into the logging's MDC filter. Mapped Diagnostic Context is essentially a map maintained by the logging framework where the application code provides key-value pairs which can then be inserted by the logging framework in log messages. MDC data can also be highly helpful in filtering messages or triggering certain actions.

docs.name: cas.logging.mdc.headers-to-exclude
docs.description: A list of headers to exclude. This list is used to specify parameters that should be excluded from MDC logging. The parameter names can be specified as regular expressions.

docs.name: cas.logging.mdc.parameters-to-exclude
docs.description: A list of parameters to exclude. This list is used to specify parameters that should be excluded from MDC logging. The parameter names can be specified as regular expressions.

docs.name: cas.logout.confirm-logout
docs.description: Before logout, allow the option to confirm on the web interface.

docs.name: cas.logout.follow-service-redirects
docs.description: Whether CAS should be allowed to redirect to an alternative location after logout.

docs.name: cas.logout.redirect-parameter
docs.description: The target destination to which CAS should redirect after logout is indicated and extracted by a parameter name of your choosing here. If none specified, the default will be used as {@code service}.

docs.name: cas.logout.redirect-url
docs.description: A url to which CAS must immediately redirect after all logout operations have completed. Typically useful in scenarios where CAS is acting as a proxy and needs to redirect to an external identity provider's logout endpoint in order to remove a session, etc.

docs.name: cas.message-bundle.base-names
docs.description: A list of strings representing base names for this message bundle. Set an array of basenames, each following the basic ResourceBundle convention of not specifying file extension or language codes. The resource location format is up to the specific MessageSource implementation. Regular and XMl properties files are supported: e.g. "messages" will find a "messages.properties", "messages_en.properties" etc arrangement as well as "messages.xml", "messages_en.xml" etc. The associated resource bundles will be checked sequentially when resolving a message code. Note that message definitions in a previous resource bundle will override ones in a later bundle, due to the sequential lookup.

docs.name: cas.message-bundle.cache-seconds
docs.description: Cache size.

docs.name: cas.message-bundle.common-names
docs.description:
A list of strings representing common names for this message bundle. Specify locale-independent common messages, with the message code as key and the full message String (may contain argument placeholders) as value.

Entries in last common names override first values (as opposed to baseNames used in message bundles).

docs.name: cas.message-bundle.encoding
docs.description: Message bundle character encoding.

docs.name: cas.message-bundle.fallback-system-locale
docs.description: Flag that controls whether to fallback to the default system locale if no locale is specified explicitly. Set whether to fall back to the system Locale if no files for a specific Locale have been found. If this is turned off, the only fallback will be the default file (e.g. "messages.properties" for basename "messages"). Falling back to the system Locale is the default behavior of {@link ResourceBundle}. However, this is often not desirable in an application server environment, where the system Locale is not relevant to the application at all: set this flag to {@code false} in such a scenario.

docs.name: cas.message-bundle.use-code-message
docs.description: Flag that controls whether to use code message. Set whether to use the message code as default message instead of throwing a {@code NoSuchMessageException}. Useful for development and debugging. Note: In case of a {@code MessageSourceResolvable} with multiple codes (like a FieldError) and a MessageSource that has a parent MessageSource, do not activate "useCodeAsDefaultMessage" in the parent: Else, you'll get the first code returned as message by the parent, without attempts to check further codes.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.endpoint.[key]
docs.description: Options for monitoring sensitive CAS endpoints and resources. Acts as a parent class for all endpoints and settings and exposes shortcuts so security and capability of endpoints can be globally controlled from one spot and then overridden elsewhere.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.endpoint.[key].access
docs.description:
Define the security access level of the endpoint. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code PERMIT}: Allow open access to the endpoint.
  • {@code ANONYMOUS}: Allow anonymous access to the endpoint.
  • {@code DENY}: Block access to the endpoint.
  • {@code AUTHENTICATED}: Require authenticated access to the endpoint.
  • {@code ROLE}: Require authenticated access to the endpoint along with a role requirement.
  • {@code AUTHORITY}: Require authenticated access to the endpoint along with an authority requirement.
  • {@code IP_ADDRESS}: Require authenticated access to the endpoint using a collection of IP addresses.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.endpoint.[key].required-authorities
docs.description: Required user authorities.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.endpoint.[key].required-ip-addresses
docs.description: Required IP addresses. CIDR ranges are accepted.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.endpoint.[key].required-roles
docs.description: Required user roles.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.form-login-enabled
docs.description: Control whether access to endpoints can be controlled via form-based login over the web via a special admin login endpoint.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ignored-endpoints
docs.description: List of endpoint patterns that will be added to the Spring Security's filter chain to be completed ignored and removed from security considerations and enforcements. Example: {@code /endpoint.xyz} or {@code /endpoint/**}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jaas.login-config
docs.description: JAAS login resource file.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jaas.login-context-name
docs.description:
The login context name should coincide with a given index in the login config specified. This name is used as the index to the configuration specified in the login config property.

<pre> JAASTest { org.springframework.security.authentication.jaas.TestLoginModule required; }; </pre> In the above example, {@code JAASTest} should be set as the context name.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jaas.refresh-configuration-on-startup
docs.description: If set, a call to {@code Configuration#refresh()} will be made by {@code #configureJaas(Resource)} method.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.autocommit
docs.description: The default auto-commit behavior of connections in the pool. Determined whether queries such as update/insert should be immediately executed without waiting for an underlying transaction.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.batch-size
docs.description: A non-zero value enables use of JDBC2 batch updates by Hibernate. e.g. recommended values between 5 and 30.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.connection-timeout
docs.description: Indicates the maximum number of milliseconds that the service can wait to obtain a connection.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.data-source-name
docs.description: Attempts to do a JNDI data source look up for the data source name specified. Will attempt to locate the data source object as is.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.default-catalog
docs.description: Qualifies unqualified table names with the given catalog in generated SQL.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.default-schema
docs.description: Qualify unqualified table names with the given schema/tablespace in generated SQL.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.dialect
docs.description: The database dialect is a configuration setting for platform independent software (JPA, Hibernate, etc) which allows such software to translate its generic SQL statements into vendor specific DDL, DML.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.driver-class
docs.description: The JDBC driver used to connect to the database.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.fetch-size
docs.description: Used to specify number of rows to be fetched in a select query.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.generate-statistics
docs.description: Allow hibernate to generate query statistics.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.health-query
docs.description: The SQL query to be executed to test the validity of connections. This is for "legacy" databases that do not support the JDBC4 {@code Connection.isValid()} API.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.idle-timeout
docs.description: Controls the maximum amount of time that a connection is allowed to sit idle in the pool.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.isolate-internal-queries
docs.description:
This property determines whether data source isolates internal pool queries, such as the connection alive test, in their own transaction.

Since these are typically read-only queries, it is rarely necessary to encapsulate them in their own transaction. This property only applies if {@link #autocommit} is disabled.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.isolation-level-name
docs.description: Defines the isolation level for transactions. @see org.springframework.transaction.TransactionDefinition

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.leak-threshold
docs.description: Controls the amount of time that a connection can be out of the pool before a message is logged indicating a possible connection leak.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password
docs.description: The database connection password.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.character-encoding
docs.description: The encoding algorithm to use such as 'UTF-8'. Relevant when the type used is {@code DEFAULT}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.encoding-algorithm
docs.description: The encoding algorithm to use such as {@code MD5}. Relevant when the type used is {@code DEFAULT} or {@code GLIBC_CRYPT}. When used with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, it should be one of {@code PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1}, {@code PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256} or {@code PBKDF2WithHmacSHA512}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.hash-length
docs.description: When used by {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#ARGON2}, it indicates the hash strength/length.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.iterations
docs.description: When used by {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, it indicates the required number of iterations.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.secret
docs.description: Secret to use with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#STANDARD}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#BCRYPT}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#GLIBC_CRYPT} password encoders. Secret usually is an optional setting.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.strength
docs.description: Strength or number of iterations to use for password hashing. Usually relevant when dealing with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#BCRYPT}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2} or {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#GLIBC_CRYPT}. When used by {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#ARGON2} or {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, it indicates the salt strength.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.password-encoder.type
docs.description:
Define the password encoder type to use. Type may be specified as blank or {@code NONE} to disable password encoding. It may also refer to a fully-qualified class name that implements the Spring Security's {@code PasswordEncoder} interface if you wish you define your own encoder.

The following types may be used:

  • {@code NONE}: No password encoding (i.e. plain-text) takes place.
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Use the {@code DefaultPasswordEncoder} of CAS. For message-digest algorithms via {@code character-encoding} and {@code encoding-algorithm}.
  • {@code BCRYPT}: Use the {@code BCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code SCRYPT}: Use the {@code SCryptPasswordEncoder}.
  • {@code PBKDF2}: Use the {@code Pbkdf2PasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code STANDARD}: Use the {@code StandardPasswordEncoder} based on the secret provided.
  • {@code SSHA}: Use the {@code LdapShaPasswordEncoder} supports Ldap SHA and SSHA (salted-SHA). The values are base-64 encoded and have the label {SHA} or {SSHA} prepended to the encoded hash.
  • {@code GLIBC_CRYPT}: Use the {@code GlibcCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the {@code encoding-algorithm}, strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code org.example.MyEncoder}: An implementation of {@code PasswordEncoder} of your own choosing.
  • {@code file:///path/to/script.groovy}: Path to a Groovy script charged with handling password encoding operations.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.physical-naming-strategy-class-name
docs.description: Fully-qualified name of the class that can control the physical naming strategy of hibernate.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.keep-alive-time
docs.description: This property controls the keepalive interval for a connection in the pool. An in-use connection will never be tested by the keepalive thread, only when it is idle will it be tested. Default is zero, which disables this feature.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.max-size
docs.description: Controls the maximum number of connections to keep in the pool, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.max-wait
docs.description:
Sets the maximum time in seconds that this data source will wait while attempting to connect to a database.

A value of zero specifies that the timeout is the default system timeout if there is one; otherwise, it specifies that there is no timeout.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.maximum-lifetime
docs.description: This property controls the maximum lifetime of a connection in the pool. When a connection reaches this timeout, even if recently used, it will be retired from the pool. An in-use connection will never be retired, only when it is idle will it be removed.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.min-size
docs.description: Controls the minimum size that the pool is allowed to reach, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.name
docs.description: Set the name of the connection pool. This is primarily used for the MBean to uniquely identify the pool configuration.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.suspension
docs.description:
Whether or not pool suspension is allowed.

There is a performance impact when pool suspension is enabled. Unless you need it (for a redundancy system for example) do not enable it.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.pool.timeout-millis
docs.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that the pool will wait for a connection to be validated as alive.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.propagation-behavior-name
docs.description: Defines the propagation behavior for transactions. @see org.springframework.transaction.TransactionDefinition

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.properties
docs.description: Additional settings provided by Hibernate (or the connection provider) in form of key-value pairs.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.query
docs.description: Query to execute in order to authenticate users via JDBC. Example: {@code SELECT username,password,enabled FROM users WHERE username=?}

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.read-only
docs.description: Configures the Connections to be added to the pool as read-only Connections.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.role-prefix
docs.description: Prefix to add to the role.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.url
docs.description: The database connection URL.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.jdbc.user
docs.description:
The database user.

The database user must have sufficient permissions to be able to handle schema changes and updates, when needed.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.json.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.allow-multiple-dns
docs.description: Whether search/query results are allowed to match on multiple DNs, or whether a single unique DN is expected for the result.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.allow-multiple-entries
docs.description: Set if multiple Entries are allowed.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.base-dn
docs.description: Base DN to use. There may be scenarios where different parts of a single LDAP tree could be considered as base-dns. Rather than duplicating the LDAP configuration block for each individual base-dn, each entry can be specified and joined together using a special delimiter character. The user DN is retrieved using the combination of all base-dn and DN resolvers in the order defined. DN resolution should fail if multiple DNs are found. Otherwise the first DN found is returned. Usual syntax is: {@code subtreeA,dc=example,dc=net|subtreeC,dc=example,dc=net}.

  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} provided - Use the provided credentials to bind when initializing connections.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to {@code *} - Use a fast-bind strategy to initialize the pool.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to blank - Skip connection initializing; perform operations anonymously.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.connection-strategy

  • {@code ROUND_ROBIN} For each new connection the next url in the list will be used.
  • {@code RANDOM} For each new connection a random LDAP url will be selected.
  • {@code DNS_SRV} LDAP urls based on DNS SRV records of the configured/given LDAP url will be used.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.principal-attribute-password
docs.description:
If principalAttributePassword is empty then a user simple bind is done to validate credentials otherwise the given attribute is compared with the given principalAttributePassword using the SHA encrypted value of it.

For the anonymous authentication type, if principalAttributePassword is empty then a user simple bind is done to validate credentials otherwise the given attribute is compared with the given principalAttributePassword using the SHA encrypted value of it.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.search-entry-handlers[].type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

  • {@code ANY}: Trust any client or server.

docs.name: cas.monitor.endpoints.ldap.type
docs.description:
The authentication type.
  • {@code AD} - Users authenticate with {@code sAMAccountName}.
  • {@code AUTHENTICATED} - Manager bind/search type of authentication. If {@code} principalAttributePassword} is empty then a user simple bind is done to validate credentials. Otherwise the given attribute is compared with the given {@code principalAttributePassword} using the {@code SHA} encrypted value of it.
  • {@code ANONYMOUS}: Similar semantics as {@code AUTHENTICATED} except no {@code bindDn} and {@code bindCredential} may be specified to initialize the connection. If {@code principalAttributePassword} is empty then a user simple bind is done to validate credentials. Otherwise the given attribute is compared with the given {@code principalAttributePassword} using the {@code SHA} encrypted value of it.
  • DIRECT: Direct Bind - Compute user DN from format string and perform simple bind. This is relevant when no search is required to compute the DN needed for a bind operation. Use cases for this type are: 1) All users are under a single branch in the directory, {@code e.g. ou=Users,dc=example,dc=org.} 2) The username provided on the CAS login form is part of the DN, e.g. {@code uid=%s,ou=Users,dc=example,dc=org}.
Available values are as follows:
  • {@code AD}: Active Directory.
  • {@code AUTHENTICATED}: Authenticated Search.
  • {@code DIRECT}: Direct Bind.
  • {@code ANONYMOUS}: Anonymous Search.

  • {@code none}: No validation takes place.

docs.name: cas.monitor.jdbc.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.monitor.jdbc.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

By default the pool will block indefinitely and there is no guarantee that

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].connection-strategy
docs.description:
If multiple URLs are provided as the ldapURL this describes how each URL will be processed.
  • {@code ACTIVE_PASSIVE} First LDAP will be used for every request unless it fails and then the next shall be used.
  • {@code ROUND_ROBIN} For each new connection the next url in the list will be used.
  • {@code RANDOM} For each new connection a random LDAP url will be selected.
  • {@code DNS_SRV} LDAP urls based on DNS SRV records of the configured/given LDAP url will be used.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.keep-alive-time
docs.description:
This property controls the keepalive interval for a connection in the pool. An in-use connection
will never be tested by the keepalive thread, only when it is idle will it be tested.
Default is zero, which disables this feature.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.max-size
docs.description:
Controls the maximum number of connections to keep
in the pool, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.max-wait
docs.description:
Sets the maximum time in seconds that this data source will wait while attempting to connect to a database.

A value of zero specifies that the timeout is the default system timeout if there is one; otherwise, it specifies that there is no timeout.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.maximum-lifetime
docs.description:
This property controls the maximum lifetime of a connection in the pool. When a connection
reaches this timeout, even if recently used,
it will be retired from the pool. An in-use connection will never be retired, only when it is idle will it be removed.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.min-size
docs.description:
Controls the minimum size that the pool is allowed
to reach, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.name
docs.description:
Set the name of the connection pool. This is primarily used for
the MBean to uniquely identify the pool configuration.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.suspension
docs.description:
Whether or not pool suspension is allowed.

There is a performance impact when pool suspension is enabled. Unless you need it (for a redundancy system for example) do not enable it.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].pool.timeout-millis
docs.description:
The maximum number of milliseconds that the
pool will wait for a connection to be validated as alive.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].prune-period
docs.description:
Removes connections from the pool based on how long they have been idle in the available queue.
Run the pruning process at the indicated interval.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].response-timeout
docs.description: Duration of time to wait for responses.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].sasl-authorization-id
docs.description: SASL authorization id.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].sasl-mechanism
docs.description: The SASL mechanism.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].sasl-mutual-auth
docs.description: Whether SASL mutual authentication is enabled.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].sasl-quality-of-protection
docs.description: SASL quality of protected.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].sasl-realm
docs.description: The SASL realm.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].sasl-security-strength
docs.description: SASL security strength.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].trust-certificates
docs.description:
Path of the trust certificates to use for the SSL connection.
Ignores keystore-related settings when activated and used.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].trust-manager
docs.description:
Trust Manager options. Trust managers are responsible for managing the trust material that is used when making LDAP trust decisions, and for deciding whether credentials presented by a peer should be accepted. Accepted values are:
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Enable and force the default JVM trust managers.
  • {@code ANY}: Trust any client or server.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].trust-store
docs.description:
Path to the keystore used to determine which certificates or
certificate authorities should be trusted.
Used when connecting to an LDAP server via LDAPS or startTLS connection.
If left blank, the default truststore for the Java runtime is used.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].trust-store-password
docs.description: Password needed to open the truststore.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].trust-store-type
docs.description:
The type of trust keystore that determines which certificates or certificate authorities are trusted.
Types depend on underlying java platform, typically {@code PKCS12} or {@code JKS}.
If left blank, defaults to the default keystore type indicated
by the underlying Java platform.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].use-start-tls
docs.description: Whether TLS should be used and enabled when establishing the connection.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validate-on-checkout
docs.description: Whether connections should be validated when loaned out from the pool.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validate-period
docs.description: Period at which pool should be validated.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validate-periodically
docs.description: Whether connections should be validated periodically when the pool is idle.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validate-timeout
docs.description: Period at which validation operations may time out.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.attribute-name
docs.description: Attribute name to use for the compare validator.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.attribute-value
docs.description: Attribute values to use for the compare validator.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.base-dn
docs.description: Base DN to use for the search request of the search validator.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.dn
docs.description: DN to compare to use for the compare validator.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.scope
docs.description: Search scope to use for the search request of the search validator.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.search-filter
docs.description: Search filter to use for the search request of the search validator.

docs.name: cas.monitor.ldap[].validator.type
docs.description:
Determine the LDAP validator type.

The following LDAP validators can be used to test connection health status:

  • {@code search}: Validates a connection is healthy by performing a search operation. Validation is considered successful if the search result size is greater than zero.
  • {@code none}: No validation takes place.
  • {@code compare}: Validates a connection is healthy by performing a compare operation.

docs.name: cas.monitor.load.warn.threshold
docs.description: The monitor threshold where if reached, CAS might generate a warning status for health checks.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.daemon
docs.description: Set the daemon state of the IO thread (defaults to true).

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.failure-mode
docs.description: Failure mode. Acceptable values are {@code Redistribute,Retry,Cancel}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.hash-algorithm
docs.description: Hash algorithm. Acceptable values are {@code NATIVE_HASH,CRC_HASH,FNV1_64_HASH,FNV1A_64_HASH,FNV1_32_HASH,FNV1A_32_HASH,KETAMA_HASH}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.kryo-auto-reset
docs.description: If true, {@code reset} is called automatically after an entire object graph has been read or written. If false, {@code reset} must be called manually, which allows unregistered class names, references, and other information to span multiple object graphs.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.kryo-objects-by-reference
docs.description: If true, each appearance of an object in the graph after the first is stored as an integer ordinal. When set to true, {@code MapReferenceResolver} is used. This enables references to the same object and cyclic graphs to be serialized, but typically adds overhead of one byte per object.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.kryo-registration-required
docs.description:
If true, an exception is thrown when an unregistered class is encountered.

If false, when an unregistered class is encountered, its fully qualified class name will be serialized and the default serializer for the class used to serialize the object. Subsequent appearances of the class within the same object graph are serialized as an int id. Registered classes are serialized as an int id, avoiding the overhead of serializing the class name, but have the drawback of needing to know the classes to be serialized up front. See {@code ComponentSerializationPlan} for help here.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.locator-type
docs.description: Locator mode. Acceptable values are {@code ARRAY_MOD, CONSISTENT, VBUCKET}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.max-idle
docs.description: Set the value for the maxTotal configuration attribute for pools created with this configuration instance.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.max-reconnect-delay
docs.description: Set the maximum reconnect delay.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.max-total
docs.description: Sets the cap on the number of objects that can be allocated by the pool (checked out to clients, or idle awaiting checkout) at a given time. Use a negative value for no limit.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.min-idle
docs.description: Get the value for the minIdle configuration attribute for pools created with this configuration instance.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.op-timeout
docs.description: Set the default operation timeout in milliseconds.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.protocol
docs.description: Protocol. Acceptable values are {@code TEXT, BINARY}.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.servers
docs.description: Comma-separated list of memcached servers.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.should-optimize
docs.description: Set to false if the default operation optimization is not desirable.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.shutdown-timeout-seconds
docs.description: The number of seconds to wait for connections to finish before shutting down the client.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.timeout-exception-threshold
docs.description: Set the maximum timeout exception threshold.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.transcoder
docs.description:
Indicate the transcoder type. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code KRYO}: CAS transcoder implementation based on Kryo fast serialization framework suited for efficient serialization of tickets. Provides pooling mechanisms as well as control over object registration and sequences.
  • {@code SERIAL}: Kryo native transcoder that serializes and compresses objects.
  • {@code WHALIN}: Transcoder that provides compatibility with Greg Whalin's memcached client.
  • {@code WHALINV1}: Handles old whalin encoding: data type is in the first byte of the value.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.transcoder-compression-threshold
docs.description: For transcoders other than kryo, determines the compression threshold. Does not apply to kryo.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memcached.use-nagle-algorithm
docs.description: Set to true if you'd like to enable the Nagle algorithm.

docs.name: cas.monitor.memory.free-mem-threshold
docs.description: The free memory threshold for the memory monitor. If the amount of free memory available reaches this point the memory monitor will report back a warning status as a health check.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo
docs.description: Options for monitoring MongoDb resources.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].authentication-database-name
docs.description: Name of the database to use for authentication.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].client-uri
docs.description:
The connection uri to the mongodb instance.
This typically takes on the form of {@code mongodb://user:psw@ds135522.somewhere.com:35522/db}.
If not specified, will fallback onto other individual settings.
If specified, takes over all other settings where applicable.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].database-name
docs.description: MongoDb database instance name.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].host
docs.description:
MongoDb database host for authentication.
Multiple host addresses may be defined, separated by comma.
If more than one host is defined, it is assumed that each host contains the port as well, if any.
Otherwise the configuration may fallback onto the port defined.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].password
docs.description: MongoDb database password for authentication.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].pool.idle-time
docs.description:
The maximum idle time of a pooled connection.  A zero value indicates no limit
to the idle time.  A pooled connection that has
exceeded its idle time will be closed and replaced when necessary by a new connection.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].pool.life-time
docs.description:
The maximum time a pooled connection can live for.  A zero value indicates no limit
to the life time.  A pooled connection that
has exceeded its life time will be closed and replaced when necessary by a new connection.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].pool.max-size
docs.description: Maximum number of connections to keep around.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].pool.max-wait-time
docs.description: The maximum time that a thread may wait for a connection to become available.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].pool.min-size
docs.description: Minimum number of connections to keep around.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].port
docs.description: MongoDb database port.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].read-concern
docs.description:
Read concern. Accepted values are:
  • {@code LOCAL}
  • {@code MAJORITY}
  • {@code LINEARIZABLE}
  • {@code SNAPSHOT}
  • {@code AVAILABLE}

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].read-preference
docs.description:
Read preference. Accepted values are:
  • {@code PRIMARY}
  • {@code SECONDARY}
  • {@code SECONDARY_PREFERRED}
  • {@code PRIMARY_PREFERRED}
  • {@code NEAREST}

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].replica-set
docs.description:
A replica set in MongoDB is a group of {@code mongod} processes that maintain
the same data set. Replica sets provide redundancy and high availability, and are the basis for all production deployments.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].retry-writes
docs.description: Sets whether writes should be retried if they fail due to a network error.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].ssl-enabled
docs.description: Whether connections require SSL.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].timeout
docs.description: MongoDb database connection timeout.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].user-id
docs.description: MongoDb database user for authentication.

docs.name: cas.monitor.mongo[].write-concern
docs.description:
Write concern describes the level of acknowledgement requested from
MongoDB for write operations to a standalone
mongo db or to replica sets or to sharded clusters. In sharded clusters,
mongo db instances will pass the write concern on to the shards.

docs.name: cas.monitor.st.warn.threshold
docs.description: The monitor threshold where if reached, CAS might generate a warning status for health checks.

docs.name: cas.monitor.tgt.warn.threshold
docs.description: The monitor threshold where if reached, CAS might generate a warning status for health checks.

docs.name: cas.monitor.warn.threshold
docs.description: The monitor threshold where if reached, CAS might generate a warning status for health checks.

docs.name: cas.multitenancy.core.enabled
docs.description: Enable multitenancy support.

docs.name: cas.multitenancy.json.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.active-attribute-repository-ids
docs.description: Activated attribute repository identifiers that should be used for fetching attributes if attribute resolution is enabled. The list here may include identifiers separated by comma.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.attribute-repository-selection
docs.description: Control the behavior of the attribute repository selection by authentication method or handler. The map here is keyed by the authentication handler name, and the value is the attribute repository identifiers separated by comma. When the authentication handler is executed, the attribute repositories assigned to this handler will be selected to fetch attributes. Note that the resolution engine will always favor attribute repositories assigned to the service definition, if any and as part of its authentication policy, over this global setting.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.attribute-resolution-enabled
docs.description:
Whether attribute repositories should be contacted to fetch person attributes. Defaults to true if not set. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-attribute
docs.description: Attribute name to use to indicate the identifier of the principal constructed. If the attribute is blank or has no values, the default principal id will be used determined by the underlying authentication engine. The principal id attribute usually is removed from the collection of attributes collected, though this behavior depends on the schematics of the underlying authentication strategy.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-resolution-conflict-strategy
docs.description: In the event that the principal resolution engine resolves more than one principal, (especially if such principals in the chain have different identifiers), this setting determines strategy by which the principal id would be chosen from the chain. Accepted values are: {@code last}, {@code first}.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-resolution-failure-fatal
docs.description:
When true, throws an error back indicating that principal resolution has failed and no principal can be found based on the authentication requirements. Otherwise, logs the condition as an error without raising a catastrophic error. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-transformation.blocking-pattern
docs.description: A regular expression that will be used against the username to match for blocking/forbidden values. If a match is found, an exception will be thrown and principal transformation will fail.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-transformation.case-conversion
docs.description:
Indicate whether the principal identifier should be transformed into upper-case, lower-case, etc. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code NONE}: No conversion.
  • {@code LOWERCASE}: Lowercase conversion.
  • {@code UPPERCASE}: Uppercase conversion.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-transformation.groovy.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-transformation.pattern
docs.description: A regular expression that will be used against the provided username for username extractions. On a successful match, the first matched group in the pattern will be used as the extracted username.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-transformation.prefix
docs.description: Prefix to add to the principal id prior to authentication.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.principal-transformation.suffix
docs.description: Suffix to add to the principal id prior to authentication.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.return-null
docs.description:
Return a null principal object if no attributes can be found for the principal. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.person-directory.use-existing-principal-id
docs.description:
Uses an existing principal id that may have already been established in order to run person directory queries. This is generally useful in situations where authentication is delegated to an external identity provider and a principal is first established to then query an attribute source. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.rest.services.attribute-name
docs.description: Authorization attribute name required by the REST endpoint in order to allow for the requested operation. Attribute must be resolvable by the authenticated principal, or must have been already.

docs.name: cas.rest.services.attribute-value
docs.description: Matching authorization attribute value, pulled from the attribute required by the REST endpoint in order to allow for the requested operation. The attribute value may also be constructed as a regex pattern.

docs.name: cas.rest.x509.body-auth
docs.description: Flag that enables {@link java.security.cert.X509Certificate} extraction from the request body for authentication.

docs.name: cas.rest.x509.header-auth
docs.description: Flag that enables {@link java.security.cert.X509Certificate} extraction from the request headers for authentication.

docs.name: cas.rest.x509.tls-client-auth
docs.description: Flag that enables TLS client {@link java.security.cert.X509Certificate} extraction from the servlet container for authentication.

docs.name: cas.saml-core.attribute-namespace
docs.description: Attribute namespace to use when generating SAML1 responses.

docs.name: cas.saml-core.issue-length
docs.description: Issue length that controls the validity period of the assertion.

docs.name: cas.saml-core.issuer
docs.description: Issuer of the assertion when generating SAML1 responses.

docs.name: cas.saml-core.persistent-id-salt
docs.description: Salt used to generate persistent or transient ids in particular when generating SAML2 responses or logout requests, etc. When left undefined, CAS will generate a random salt. For production use, it is recommended to define a salt value particularly when multiple CAS nodes are involved.

docs.name: cas.saml-core.skew-allowance
docs.description: Skew allowance that controls the issue instance of the authentication.

docs.name: cas.saml-core.ticketid-saml2
docs.description: Whether ticket ids generated should be saml2 compliant when generating SAML1 responses.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.max-validity
docs.description: If specified, creates a validity filter on the metadata to check for metadata freshness based on the max validity. Value is specified in seconds.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.parameter
docs.description: The parameter name that indicates the entity id of the service provider submitted to CAS.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.require-signed-root
docs.description: When parsing metadata, whether the root element is required to be signed.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.require-valid-metadata
docs.description: Whether valid metadata is required when parsing metadata.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.resources
docs.description: Metadata resources to load and parse through based on the incoming entity id in order to locate MDUI. Resources can be classpath/file/http resources. If each metadata resource has a signing certificate, they can be added onto the resource with a {@code ::} separator. Example: {@code classpath:/sp-metadata.xml::classpath:/pub.key}.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.schedule.cron-expression
docs.description: A cron-like expression, extending the usual UN*X definition to include triggers on the second, minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week. For example, {@code 0 * * * * MON-FRI} means once per minute on weekdays (at the top of the minute - the 0th second) or {@code 0 0 0 * * *} means every day at midnight. * Note that when cron expressions are defined, the start delay and repeat interval settings are must be removed and set to blank.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.schedule.cron-time-zone
docs.description: A time zone for which the cron expression will be resolved. By default, this attribute is empty (i.e. the scheduler's time zone will be used).

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.schedule.enabled
docs.description: Whether scheduler should be enabled to schedule the job to run.

docs.name: cas.saml-metadata-ui.schedule.enabled-on-host
docs.description: Overrides {@link SchedulingProperties#enabled} property value of true if this property does not match hostname of CAS server. This can be useful if deploying CAS with an image in a statefulset where all names are predictable but where having different configurations for different servers is hard. The value can be an exact hostname or a regular expression that will be used to match the hostname.

docs.name: cas.server.jetty.sni-host-check
docs.description: Server Name Indication is an extension of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol, which allows a client to indicate which hostname it is attempting to connect to at the start of the handshaking process. This is particularly useful when a server hosts multiple domains with different SSL certificates on a single IP address. Setting this setting to {@code false} would mean that the Jetty server will not strictly require clients to send an SNI extension during the SSL/TLS handshake and disables host name checking for Server Name Indication (SNI) during SSL/TLS handshakes.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.async-timeout
docs.description: The default timeout for asynchronous requests in milliseconds. If not specified, this attribute is set to 10000 (10 seconds).

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.attributes
docs.description:
Additional attributes to be set on the AJP connector in form of key-value pairs. Examples include:
  • {@code tomcatAuthentication}: If set to true, the authentication will be done in Tomcat. Otherwise, the authenticated principal will be propagated from the native webserver and used for authorization in Tomcat. Note that this principal will have no roles associated with it. The default value is true.
  • {@code maxThreads}: The maximum number of request processing threads to be created by this Connector, which therefore determines the maximum number of simultaneous requests that can be handled. If not specified, this attribute is set to 200. If an executor is associated with this connector, this attribute is ignored as the connector will execute tasks using the executor rather than an internal thread pool.
  • {@code keepAliveTimeout}: The number of milliseconds this Connector will wait for another AJP request before closing the connection. The default value is to use the value that has been set for the connectionTimeout attribute.
  • {@code maxCookieCount}: The maximum number of cookies that are permitted for a request. A value of less than zero means no limit. If not specified, a default value of 200 will be used.
  • {@code bufferSize}: The size of the output buffer to use. If less than or equal to zero, then output buffering is disabled. The default value is -1 (i.e. buffering disabled)
  • {@code clientCertProvider}: When client certificate information is presented in a form other than instances of java.security.cert.X509Certificate it needs to be converted before it can be used and this property controls which JSSE provider is used to perform the conversion. For example it is used with the AJP connectors, the HTTP APR connector and with the org.apache.catalina.valves.SSLValve.If not specified, the default provider will be used.
  • {@code connectionTimeout}: The number of milliseconds this Connector will wait, after accepting a connection, for the request URI line to be presented. The default value is infinite (i.e. no timeout).
  • {@code address}: For servers with more than one IP address, this attribute specifies which address will be used for listening on the specified port. By default, this port will be used on all IP addresses associated with the server. A value of 127.0.0.1 indicates that the Connector will only listen on the loopback interface.

See the Apache Tomcat documentation for a full list.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.enable-lookups
docs.description: Set to true if you want calls to {@code request.getRemoteHost()} to perform DNS lookups in order to return the actual host name of the remote client. Set to false to skip the DNS lookup and return the IP address in String form instead (thereby improving performance). By default, DNS lookups are disabled.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.enabled
docs.description: Enable AJP support in CAS for the embedded Apache Tomcat container.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.max-post-size
docs.description: The maximum size in bytes of the POST which will be handled by the container FORM URL parameter parsing. The feature can be disabled by setting this attribute to a value less than or equal to 0. If not specified, this attribute is set to 2097152 (2 megabytes).

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.port
docs.description: The TCP port number on which this Connector will create a server socket and await incoming connections. Your operating system will allow only one server application to listen to a particular port number on a particular IP address. If the special value of 0 (zero) is used, then Tomcat will select a free port at random to use for this connector. This is typically only useful in embedded and testing applications.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.protocol
docs.description: Sets the protocol to handle incoming traffic.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.proxy-port
docs.description: If this Connector is being used in a proxy configuration, configure this attribute to specify the server port to be returned for calls to request.getServerPort().

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.redirect-port
docs.description: If this Connector is supporting non-SSL requests, and a request is received for which a matching {@code security-constraint} requires SSL transport, Catalina will automatically redirect the request to the port number specified here.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.scheme
docs.description: Set this attribute to the name of the protocol you wish to have returned by calls to {@code request.getScheme()}. For example, you would set this attribute to {@code https} for an SSL Connector.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.secret
docs.description: Set the secret that must be included with every request.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.ajp.secure
docs.description: Set this attribute to true if you wish to have calls to request.isSecure() to return true for requests received by this Connector (you would want this on an SSL Connector). The default value is false.

docs.name: cas.server.tomcat.basic-authn.auth-roles
docs.description: Add an authorization role, which is a role name that will be permitted access to the resources protected by this security constraint.
